rationale: PINS THE RULING that a class EXPRESSION carrying a name is a class DECLARATION. The walk had no `case "class"` at all, so `const K = class Inner { m(){} }` was treated as a bare bag of members and lost four things at once: the Class symbol, every containment edge for its members (containment drops an edge whose owner is not a symbol, and the member extraction attributes `m` to owner `Inner`), its `extends`/`implements` heritage, and its constructor's KIND. The twins were wrong in opposite ways on the identical construct — typescript dropped the edge, javascript emitted a DANGLING `Inner->m` — and the class-expression fixture had a `forbidRelationships` pin recording that adopting the twin's edge needed a ruling on whether a class expression should be a symbol at all. This is that ruling, and that pin is now positive. Two things are pinned deliberately AGAINST: the anonymous form, which has no name to be a symbol under and so keeps its members on the binding (`Anon contains m`), and the exact counts, because the first cut of the fix extracted every member TWICE (the class extractor and the generic descent both claimed the body, since the walker's no-descend exclusion list covered `class_declaration` but never the class EXPRESSION node type) and a >=1 relationship assertion would not have noticed.

expectSymbols.name: Inner
expectSymbols.note: THE PIN. Pre-fix this class was invisible as a type, which is why its members' containment edge had an unjoinable owner.

expectSymbols.name: Recur
expectSymbols.note: The self-reference `new Recur()` already resolved to this name pre-fix — the edge pointed at a name that was not a symbol.

expectSymbols.name: constructor
expectSymbols.note: Kind, not just presence: the descent path made this a Method, so a class expression's constructor disagreed with every other form. A class DECLARATION's constructor is a Constructor.

expectSymbols.name: value
expectSymbols.note: A parameter property (`constructor(readonly value: number)`) is a declared member of the class, so it is contained by it.

expectSymbols.name: Registered
expectSymbols.note: A class expression in ARGUMENT position is still a declaration — being passed as a value does not make it anonymous.

expectSymbols.name: m
expectSymbols.note: THE COUNTER-CASE. An anonymous class expression has no name to be a symbol under, so its member belongs to the binding that holds the value. This is unchanged by the fix and pinned so the ruling cannot be over-applied.

expectRelationships.note: Heritage is clause structure; it was lost with the class and the generic oracle derives it independently.

expectRelationshipCount.note: THE DUPLICATE GUARD. The first cut of this fix ran the class extractor AND the generic descent over the same body, emitting every member and every containment edge twice. `expectRelationships` is a >=1 match and would have passed; only an exact count catches it.
Second half of the duplicate guard, on a different owner, so a fix that special-cased one class could not slip through.
